column6: Dieser Roman trifft den Zeitgeist perfekt.
column7: This novel captures the zeitgeist perfectly.
column8: Hegel turned it into a philosophical concept in the early 19th century. It entered English almost unchanged and is now used worldwide.

column6: Für diese Verhandlung braucht man echtes Fingerspitzengefühl.
column7: This negotiation calls for real tact.
column8: Literally 'fingertip feeling': it captures the German appreciation for precise, intuitive skill, in diplomacy as in medicine.

column6: Er begegnete seinem Doppelgänger auf einer Reise.
column7: He met his double on a trip.
column8: In German Romantic literature, the Doppelgänger was a supernatural alter ego. E.T.A. Hoffmann made it famous, and Freud revisited it in psychoanalysis.

column5: it is said, it says (in a text)
column6: In der Mitteilung heißt es, das Werk sei geschlossen.
column7: The statement says the plant is (reportedly) closed.
column8: 'Es heißt, ...' introduces what is said or written in a text. In reported speech the following clause often takes Konjunktiv I ('sei').

column5: coming to terms with the past
column6: Die Vergangenheitsbewältigung ist ein zentraler Teil der deutschen Identität.
column7: Coming to terms with the past is a central part of German identity.
column8: A uniquely German compound: it describes the ongoing collective process of reckoning with Nazism, through schools, memorials, and law.

column6: Ihm wird Fahrlässigkeit vorgeworfen.
column7: He is accused of negligence.
column8: In the passive with 'vorwerfen', the accusation becomes depersonalized — a move reflecting the caution of German legal and journalistic language.

column6: Das Unternehmen muss Schadenersatz leisten.
column7: The company must pay compensation.
column8: German consumer law is among the strongest in Europe: 'Schadenersatz' claims are common and culturally normal.

column6: Die Heimlichkeit des Treffens machte es aufregend.
column7: The secrecy of the meeting made it exciting.
column8: From 'heimlich' (secret, covert). The plural 'Heimlichkeiten' means little secrets; 'unheimlich' means eerie.

column6: Als Querdenker findet er immer ungewöhnliche Lösungen.
column7: As a lateral thinker, he always finds unusual solutions.
column8: Originally a positive term for creative thinkers, it was redefined in 2020-21 for anti-lockdown movements — a striking case of semantic drift under political pressure.

column6: Ein tiefer Weltschmerz lag in seinen Augen.
column7: A deep world-weariness lay in his eyes.
column8: Coined by Jean Paul in 1827, it describes the pain of the gap between reality and ideals — a central concept of German Romanticism.

column6: Das ist beileibe nicht die einzige Erklärung.
column7: That is by no means the only explanation.
column8: An emphatic, learned-register expression, where 'bei Leibe' ('by [my] body') is an old oath fossilized into the language.

column6: Der zu erwartende Widerstand der Anwohner wurde unterschätzt.
column7: The resistance to be expected from residents was underestimated.
column8: The extended participle ('zu erwartende') compresses a whole relative clause before the noun — a hallmark of German administrative prose.

column6: Die Wohnung wurde unterderhand vergeben.
column7: The apartment was handed out on the quiet.
column8: A very concrete image: 'under the hand', i.e. outside official channels, often to whoever knows the right people.

column6: Die Reform ist eine Gratwanderung zwischen Sparen und Investieren.
column7: The reform is a delicate balancing act between saving and investing.
column8: An alpine image: the 'Grat' is a mountain's exposed ridge. Walking it means proceeding with a drop on either side.

column6: Wir fahren morgen los, es sei denn, das Wetter wird schlechter.
column7: We're leaving tomorrow, unless the weather gets worse.
column8: A fossil of Konjunktiv I ('sei'): the phrase has crystallized and stays alive even where the subjunctive has otherwise disappeared.

column6: Diese Arbeitsbedingungen sind eine Zumutung.
column7: These working conditions are an outrage.
column8: From 'jemandem etwas zumuten' (to ask too much of someone): calling something 'eine Zumutung' is a strong but composed protest.

column6: Eine Lösung zeichnet sich langsam ab.
column7: A solution is slowly becoming apparent.
column8: A graphic image: something 'sketching itself' on the horizon, still vague but already recognizable. Frequent in political analysis.

column6: Die Aussicht war geradezu atemberaubend.
column7: The view was downright breathtaking.
column8: An intensifier signaling 'this word sounds exaggerated but it's the right one' — typical of essayistic prose.

column6: Die Tragweite dieser Entscheidung war anfangs nicht absehbar.
column7: The scope of this decision wasn't foreseeable at first.
column8: Literally 'how far it carries': used for decisions and laws whose consequences extend well beyond the present moment.

column6: Er versuchte, die Zahlen zu beschönigen.
column7: He tried to gloss over the figures.
column8: From 'schön' (beautiful): making something 'prettier' than it is. A recurring accusation in political and environmental debate.

column6: Die vermeintliche Abkürzung kostete uns eine Stunde.
column7: The supposed shortcut cost us an hour.
column8: Signals skepticism: saying 'vermeintlich' hints that the expectation turned out to be wrong.

column6: Das Jahr 1989 war eine tiefe Zäsur in der europäischen Geschichte.
column7: 1989 was a deep caesura in European history.
column8: A loanword from Latin via poetic meter: it denotes a break so clean that the 'after' no longer resembles the 'before'.

column5: in the course of / as part of
column6: Im Zuge der Renovierung wurde auch das Dach erneuert.
column7: In the course of the renovation, the roof was also redone.
column8: Takes the genitive: 'im Zuge der Renovierung'. Here 'Zug' is not the train but 'course, progress': it means 'in the course of'.

column6: In der Debatte lag eine unterschwellige Aggressivität.
column7: There was a subliminal aggressiveness in the debate.
column8: Literally 'below the threshold' (Schwelle) of conscious perception: applied to tones, tensions, and advertising messages.

column6: Der mutmaßliche Täter wurde festgenommen.
column7: The alleged perpetrator was arrested.
column8: 'Mutmaßlich' comes from 'Mutmaßung' (conjecture): used in legal and journalistic language to avoid implying proven guilt.

column6: Seine Kompetenz ist unumstritten.
column7: His expertise is undisputed.
column8: 'Unumstritten' combines the negative prefix 'un-' and 'umstritten' (controversial): literally 'not controversial'.

column5: par excellence / in the truest sense
column6: Er gilt als Experte schlechthin auf diesem Gebiet.
column7: He's considered the expert par excellence in this field.
column8: 'Schlechthin' always follows the noun it modifies and expresses an absolute, definitive statement.

column6: Das ist die Stadt der Kunst par excellence.
column7: That is the city of art par excellence.
column8: A direct loanword from French, used in a learned register to underline absolute excellence.

column6: Man geht gemeinhin davon aus, dass dies stimmt.
column7: It's generally assumed that this is true.
column8: 'Davon ausgehen' takes a conceptual genitive via 'davon' and means 'to presuppose, take as a given'.

column6: Die Bedingungen sind erfüllt, mithin ist der Vertrag gültig.
column7: The conditions are met, therefore the contract is valid.
column8: 'Mithin' is a formal/legal connective, an elegant alternative to 'also' or 'deshalb'.

column6: Die Nachfrage stieg, infolgedessen erhöhten sich die Preise.
column7: Demand rose, and as a result prices increased.
column8: 'Infolgedessen' combines 'infolge' (as a result of) and 'dessen' (genitive of 'das'): a formal logical consequence.

column6: Der Plan ist riskant, gleichwohl verspricht er hohen Gewinn.
column7: The plan is risky, yet it promises high profit.
column8: 'Gleichwohl' is an elegant, literary variant of 'trotzdem' or 'dennoch', typical of formal writing.

column6: Es regnete, nichtsdestotrotz gingen sie wandern.
column7: It was raining, but nonetheless they went hiking.
column8: 'Nichtsdestotrotz' is a colloquial-literary formation intensifying 'nichtsdestoweniger', often used with an ironic tone.

column6: Das war fürwahr ein denkwürdiger Tag.
column7: That was truly a memorable day.
column8: 'Fürwahr' is an archaic adverb, today used almost only ironically or literarily to emphasize a statement.

column6: Das ist mitnichten die einzige Erklärung.
column7: That is by no means the only explanation.
column8: 'Mitnichten' is an emphatic, high-register negation, a formal alternative to 'keineswegs'.

column6: Das ist keineswegs sicher.
column7: That is by no means certain.
column8: 'Keineswegs' is the standard emphatic negation of formal written register, more common than 'mitnichten'.

column6: Insofern hat er recht.
column7: In that respect he's right.
column8: 'Insofern' can also introduce a subordinate clause with 'als': 'insofern, als...' ('to the extent that...').

column6: Diesbezüglich gibt es noch offene Fragen.
column7: In this regard there are still open questions.
column8: 'Diesbezüglich' combines 'dies' (this) and 'bezüglich' (regarding): a connective typical of formal correspondence.

column6: Die Frist ist nunmehr abgelaufen.
column7: The deadline has now expired.
column8: 'Nunmehr' is a formal variant of 'jetzt', typical of legal and administrative language.

column6: Hier ist rasches Handeln vonnöten.
column7: Swift action is required here.
column8: 'Vonnöten sein' is an archaic-formal construction equivalent to 'nötig sein', still used in elevated writing.

column6: Die Entscheidung obliegt dem Vorstand.
column7: The decision is incumbent upon the board.
column8: 'Obliegen' takes the dative of the person or entity responsible, a verb typical of legal language.

column6: Der Vertrag gewährleistet volle Transparenz.
column7: The contract guarantees full transparency.
column8: 'Gewährleisten' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, a formal verb typical of contracts and regulations.

column6: Die Studie untermauert diese These.
column7: The study substantiates this thesis.
column8: 'Untermauern' comes from 'Mauer' (wall): literally 'to reinforce with a wall underneath', i.e. giving an argument solid grounding.

column6: Die Kommission konstatiert erhebliche Mängel.
column7: The commission finds significant shortcomings.
column8: 'Konstatieren' is a loanword from French, used formally to state an objectively observed fact.

column6: Die Theorie postuliert einen direkten Zusammenhang.
column7: The theory postulates a direct connection.
column8: 'Postulieren' is an academic-philosophical term, used to propose a principle without directly proving it.

column6: Ich muss konzedieren, dass Sie recht haben.
column7: I must concede that you're right.
column8: 'Konzedieren' is a very formal term, almost exclusive to academic or diplomatic register, rarely used in speech.

column6: Der Kommentar insinuiert Fehlverhalten.
column7: The comment insinuates misconduct.
column8: 'Insinuieren' is a high-register loanword from Latin, used for implicit accusation without stating it directly.

column6: Das Ministerium dementiert die Vorwürfe.
column7: The ministry officially denies the accusations.
column8: 'Dementieren' is typical of journalistic and institutional language for an official, public denial.

column6: Er musste seine Meinung revidieren.
column7: He had to revise his opinion.
column8: 'Revidieren' is a learned Latin loanword, more formal than the plain 'ändern' (to change).

column6: Man sollte diese Aussage relativieren.
column7: This statement should be put into perspective.
column8: 'Relativieren' means softening the absoluteness of a claim, a term typical of critical and academic discourse.

column6: Ihre Kritik ist gut nuanciert.
column7: Her critique is well nuanced.
column8: 'Nuancieren' is a loanword from French, used academically and critically to describe argumentative subtlety.

column6: Die Zahlen kaschieren das eigentliche Problem.
column7: The figures mask the real problem.
column8: 'Kaschieren' is a loanword from French, used to describe skillfully hiding something negative.

column6: Der Titel suggeriert eine falsche Schlussfolgerung.
column7: The headline suggests a false conclusion.
column8: 'Suggerieren' is a Latin loanword, used to describe a subtle, often manipulative implication.

column6: Gute Strategen antizipieren Probleme.
column7: Good strategists anticipate problems.
column8: 'Antizipieren' is a formal term, a learned alternative to the more common 'vorhersehen' (to foresee).

column6: Dieses Argument impliziert eine bestimmte Weltsicht.
column7: This argument implies a certain worldview.
column8: 'Implizieren' is a logical-philosophical term, used for a necessary consequence, not just a suggested one.

column6: Man muss zwischen den beiden Begriffen differenzieren.
column7: One must differentiate between the two concepts.
column8: 'Differenzieren zwischen' takes the dative: 'zwischen den Begriffen' — a structure typical of academic register.

column6: Das Konzept muss noch ausdifferenziert werden.
column7: The concept still needs to be elaborated in detail.
column8: 'Ausdifferenziert werden' is passive, common in academic language for a concept still under development.

column6: Das ist ein klassischer Trugschluss.
column7: That's a classic fallacy.
column8: 'Trugschluss' combines 'Trug' (deception) and 'Schluss' (conclusion): a logical conclusion that's deceptive but seemingly valid.

column6: Diese Argumentation ist ein Zirkelschluss.
column7: This argument is circular reasoning.
column8: 'Zirkelschluss' combines 'Zirkel' (circle) and 'Schluss' (conclusion): an argument that presupposes what it seeks to prove.

column6: Das ist ein häufiger Denkfehler.
column7: That's a common thinking error.
column8: 'Denkfehler' combines 'Denken' (thinking) and 'Fehler' (error): an error in the thought process itself, not in the facts.

column6: Seine Voreiligkeit führte zu Fehlern.
column7: His hastiness led to mistakes.
column8: 'Voreiligkeit' comes from 'voreilig' (rash), literally 'hurrying before the time'.

column6: In der Krise bewahrte sie Besonnenheit.
column7: In the crisis she kept a level head.
column8: 'Besonnenheit' comes from 'besonnen' (level-headed, prudent), the direct opposite of 'Voreiligkeit'.

column6: Er handelte mit großer Umsicht.
column7: He acted with great circumspection.
column8: 'Umsicht' combines 'um' (around) and 'Sicht' (view): literally 'looking around' before acting, i.e. with care.

column6: Der Sachverhalt muss genau geprüft werden.
column7: The facts of the matter must be carefully examined.
column8: 'Geprüft werden' is passive, typical of legal and administrative language for a formal review.

column6: Angesichts der Sachlage ist Vorsicht geboten.
column7: Given the situation, caution is called for.
column8: 'Angesichts' takes the genitive and is typical of formal-administrative register.

column6: Das Gutachten bestätigt die Sicherheitsbedenken.
column7: The expert report confirms the safety concerns.
column8: 'Gutachten' combines 'gut' and 'achten' (to observe well): a formal technical assessment carried out by an expert.

column6: Der Vollzug der Strafe beginnt nächste Woche.
column7: The serving of the sentence begins next week.
column8: From 'vollziehen'. Legal term: 'Strafvollzug' means the prison system. For a judgement, 'Vollstreckung' is more usual.

column6: Das Urteil ist mittlerweile rechtskräftig.
column7: The ruling is now legally binding.
column8: 'Rechtskräftig' combines 'Recht' and 'Kraft' (force): a decision that has acquired full, final legal force.

column6: Der Anwalt legt Berufung ein.
column7: The lawyer is filing an appeal.
column8: 'Einlegen' is separable and takes the accusative: 'Berufung einlegen' is the standard fixed collocation in German law.

column6: Die Beweislast liegt beim Kläger.
column7: The burden of proof lies with the plaintiff.
column8: 'Liegen bei' takes the dative: 'beim Kläger' — a fixed legal structure for indicating who bears a responsibility.

column6: Die Zeugenaussage widersprach der offiziellen Version.
column7: The witness testimony contradicted the official version.
column8: 'Widersprechen' takes the dative: 'der offiziellen Version', a verb with the always-inseparable prefix 'wider-'.

column6: Das Urteil basiert auf Indizienbeweisen.
column7: The verdict is based on circumstantial evidence.
column8: 'Basieren auf' takes the dative: 'auf Indizienbeweisen' — a common fixed structure in legal and journalistic discourse.

column6: Sein Geständnis führte zu einer Strafmilderung.
column7: His confession led to a mitigation of sentence.
column8: 'Strafmilderung' combines 'Strafe' (penalty) and 'Milderung' (mitigation), a technical criminal-law term.

column6: Die Rechtsauffassung der Richter unterscheidet sich.
column7: The judges' legal opinions differ.
column8: 'Rechtsauffassung' combines 'Recht' and 'Auffassung' (view, interpretation), typical of courtroom language.

column6: Diese Vertragsklausel ist ungewöhnlich streng.
column7: This contract clause is unusually strict.
column8: 'Ungewöhnlich' means 'unusual', often used as an intensifier for adjectives in formal register.

column6: Sie haben keinen Rechtsanspruch darauf.
column7: They have no legal claim to it.
column8: 'Rechtsanspruch' combines 'Recht' and 'Anspruch' (claim, entitlement), a formal legal term.

column6: Die Firma übernimmt keine Haftung für Schäden.
column7: The company accepts no liability for damages.
column8: 'Haftung übernehmen' is the standard fixed collocation, often seen in liability disclaimers.

column6: Grobe Fahrlässigkeit wird nicht durch die Police gedeckt.
column7: Gross negligence isn't covered by the policy.
column8: 'Gedeckt werden' is passive, common in insurance language for describing what falls under coverage.

column6: Ärzte unterliegen einer besonderen Sorgfaltspflicht.
column7: Doctors are subject to a special duty of care.
column8: 'Unterliegen' takes the dative: 'einer Sorgfaltspflicht', a formal inseparable verb used in law.

column6: Dieses Urteil könnte einen Präzedenzfall schaffen.
column7: This ruling could set a precedent.
column8: 'Präzedenzfall' combines the Latin loanword 'Präzedenz' and 'Fall' (case): a case that sets a model for the future.

column6: Die Firma nutzt eine Gesetzeslücke aus.
column7: The company is exploiting a legal loophole.
column8: 'Ausnutzen' is separable and takes the accusative, often with a critical connotation when talking about exploiting gaps in the law.

column6: Die Novellierung des Gesetzes wird diskutiert.
column7: The amendment of the law is being discussed.
column8: 'Novellierung' comes from the Latin 'novella lex' (new law): the formal process of updating an existing law.

column6: Das Inkrafttreten ist für Januar geplant.
column7: Entry into force is planned for January.
column8: 'Inkrafttreten' is the nominalized infinitive of 'in Kraft treten' (to take effect), always neuter like all nominalized infinitives.

column6: Es gibt eine Übergangsregelung für Altverträge.
column7: There's a transitional arrangement for old contracts.
column8: 'Übergangsregelung' combines 'Übergang' (transition) and 'Regelung' (regulation), typical of legislative reforms.

column6: Verbraucher haben ein gesetzliches Widerspruchsrecht.
column7: Consumers have a statutory right to object.
column8: 'Widerspruchsrecht' combines 'Widerspruch' (objection) and 'Recht' (right), a key term in consumer protection.

column6: Die Datenerhebung erfolgt anonymisiert.
column7: Data collection happens anonymously.
column8: 'Erfolgen' is a formal intransitive verb meaning 'to take place', used in institutional and technical contexts.

column6: Zweckbindung ist ein Grundprinzip des Datenschutzes.
column7: Purpose limitation is a basic principle of data protection.
column8: 'Zweckbindung' combines 'Zweck' (purpose) and 'Bindung' (binding), a key principle of the European GDPR.

column6: Ohne Einwilligung dürfen Daten nicht verarbeitet werden.
column7: Without consent, data may not be processed.
column8: 'Dürfen ... nicht' expresses negated permission, while 'verarbeitet werden' is passive.

column6: Jeder hat ein Auskunftsrecht über seine Daten.
column7: Everyone has a right to information about their data.
column8: 'Auskunftsrecht' combines 'Auskunft' (information) and 'Recht' (right), a pillar of European privacy law.

column6: Der Löschungsanspruch gilt nur unter bestimmten Bedingungen.
column7: The right to erasure applies only under certain conditions.
column8: 'Unter bestimmten Bedingungen' uses the dative: 'gelten unter' — a fixed structure in legal language.

column6: Compliance ist in Banken besonders wichtig.
column7: Compliance is especially important in banks.
column8: A direct English loanword, now standard in German corporate and financial language.

column6: Der Whistleblower deckte den Skandal auf.
column7: The whistleblower uncovered the scandal.
column8: 'Aufdecken' is separable and takes the accusative: 'deckte auf' in the Präteritum, meaning 'to uncover, bring to light'.

column6: Eine sorgfältige Interessenabwägung ist notwendig.
column7: A careful balancing of interests is necessary.
column8: 'Interessenabwägung' combines 'Interesse' (interest) and 'Abwägung' (weighing), a central legal term in assessing rights.

column6: Die Auslegung des Gesetzes ist umstritten.
column7: The interpretation of the law is disputed.
column8: 'Auslegung' comes from 'auslegen' (to interpret, expound), a formal term used both legally and biblically.

column6: Der öffentliche Diskurs hat sich verschärft.
column7: Public discourse has become harsher.
column8: 'Diskurs' is more technical-academic than 'Gespräch' or 'Debatte', often used in philosophy and the social sciences.

column6: Wer die Diskurshoheit hat, bestimmt die Debatte.
column7: Whoever holds discourse dominance determines the debate.
column8: 'Diskurshoheit' combines 'Diskurs' and 'Hoheit' (sovereignty), referring to who controls the terms of a public debate.

column6: Dieses Narrativ wird zunehmend hinterfragt.
column7: This narrative is increasingly being questioned.
column8: 'Hinterfragt werden' is passive, common for describing the questioning of a dominant discourse.

column6: Beide Seiten nutzen unterschiedliche Deutungsmuster.
column7: Both sides use different interpretive patterns.
column8: 'Deutungsmuster' combines 'Deutung' (interpretation) and 'Muster' (pattern), a key term in sociology.

column6: Ein neues wissenschaftliches Paradigma setzte sich durch.
column7: A new scientific paradigm prevailed.
column8: 'Sich durchsetzen' is separable and reflexive, meaning 'to prevail', used for dominant ideas or trends.

column6: Die Erfindung war ein echter Paradigmenwechsel.
column7: The invention was a true paradigm shift.
column8: 'Paradigmenwechsel' combines 'Paradigma' and 'Wechsel' (change), a concept made famous by philosopher Thomas Kuhn.

column6: Er stellt jedes Dogma infrage.
column7: He questions every dogma.
column8: 'Infrage stellen' means 'to question', a fixed phrase sometimes also written 'in Frage stellen'.

column6: Dogmatismus verhindert offenen Diskurs.
column7: Dogmatism prevents open discourse.
column8: 'Verhindern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to prevent', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Reduktionismus vereinfacht komplexe Phänomene zu stark.
column7: Reductionism oversimplifies complex phenomena.
column8: 'Zu stark' reinforces 'vereinfachen' (to simplify), indicating a critical excess.

column6: Der Determinismus stellt den freien Willen infrage.
column7: Determinism calls free will into question.
column8: 'Infrage stellen' is a fixed phrase meaning 'to call into doubt, question'.

column6: Die Frage nach dem freien Willen bleibt offen.
column7: The question of free will remains open.
column8: 'Die Frage nach' takes the dative: 'nach dem freien Willen' — a fixed structure for introducing a philosophical question.

column6: Der Existenzialismus betont die individuelle Verantwortung.
column7: Existentialism emphasizes individual responsibility.
column8: Twentieth-century philosophical movement (Sartre, Heidegger). The spelling 'Existentialismus' also occurs; the adjective is 'existenzialistisch'.

column6: Nihilismus verneint jeden objektiven Sinn.
column7: Nihilism denies any objective meaning.
column8: 'Verneinen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to deny', a formal philosophical term.

column6: Die Absolutheit dieser Aussage überzeugt mich nicht.
column7: The absoluteness of this statement doesn't convince me.
column8: 'Absolutheit' comes from 'absolut' with the abstract suffix '-heit', a high-register philosophical term.

column6: Kultureller Relativismus wird oft kritisiert.
column7: Cultural relativism is often criticized.
column8: 'Kritisiert werden' is passive, common in academic discourse for describing contested positions.

column6: Die Dialektik von These und Antithese führt zur Synthese.
column7: The dialectic of thesis and antithesis leads to synthesis.
column8: The Hegelian dialectical method (thesis-antithesis-synthesis) is central to classical German philosophy.

column6: Die Synthese der beiden Positionen gelang gut.
column7: The synthesis of the two positions worked well.
column8: 'Gelingen' takes the dative of the person who succeeds at something — an inverted construction compared to English.

column6: Die Kontingenz historischer Ereignisse wird oft unterschätzt.
column7: The contingency of historical events is often underestimated.
column8: 'Unterschätzt werden' is passive, used to describe phenomena not adequately acknowledged.

column6: Korrelation bedeutet nicht automatisch Kausalität.
column7: Correlation doesn't automatically mean causality.
column8: A classic distinction in scientific method: 'Korrelation' doesn't necessarily imply 'Kausalität'.

column6: Diese Behauptung stützt sich nicht auf Empirie.
column7: This claim isn't based on empirical evidence.
column8: 'Sich stützen auf' takes the accusative: 'auf Empirie' — a fixed structure indicating the basis of an argument.

column6: Die These lässt sich empirisch belegen.
column7: The thesis can be substantiated empirically.
column8: 'Sich belegen lassen' expresses passive possibility: 'lets itself be proven', i.e. 'can be proven'.

column6: Falsifizierbarkeit ist laut Popper ein Kriterium für Wissenschaftlichkeit.
column7: Falsifiability is, according to Popper, a criterion for being scientific.
column8: Karl Popper's criterion of 'Falsifizierbarkeit' is central to modern philosophy of science.

column6: Erkenntnistheorie fragt, wie wir wissen können, was wir wissen.
column7: Epistemology asks how we can know what we know.
column8: 'Erkenntnistheorie' combines 'Erkenntnis' (knowledge) and 'Theorie' (theory), the philosophical branch on the nature of knowledge.

column6: Die Diskussion wechselt oft auf eine Metaebene.
column7: The discussion often shifts to a meta-level.
column8: 'Metaebene' combines the Greek prefix 'Meta-' (beyond) and 'Ebene' (level): a level of reflection on the discussion itself.

column6: Die Immanenz Gottes ist ein zentrales theologisches Thema.
column7: God's immanence is a central theological topic.
column8: 'Immanenz' contrasts with 'Transzendenz' (transcendence), a key conceptual pair in religious philosophy.

column6: Viele Religionen betonen die Transzendenz des Göttlichen.
column7: Many religions emphasize the transcendence of the divine.
column8: 'Das Göttliche' is a nominalized neuter adjective: 'the divine' as an abstract noun.

column6: Man kann ein System auch immanent kritisieren.
column7: One can also criticize a system immanently.
column8: 'Immanent' as an adverb describes a critique that accepts a system's premises in order to refute it from within.

column6: Der Text endet in einer echten Aporie.
column7: The text ends in a genuine aporia.
column8: 'Aporie' comes from ancient Greek and describes an apparently unsolvable philosophical dilemma.

column6: Kant beschreibt vier klassische Antinomien.
column7: Kant describes four classic antinomies.
column8: The concept of 'Antinomie' is central to Kantian philosophy, referring to two contradictory yet equally provable propositions.

column6: Der Kategorische Imperativ ist Kants zentrales ethisches Prinzip.
column7: The categorical imperative is Kant's central ethical principle.
column8: A fundamental concept of Immanuel Kant's moral philosophy, among the most influential German philosophical contributions in the world.

column6: Die Phänomenologie untersucht das Erleben selbst.
column7: Phenomenology studies lived experience itself.
column8: Phenomenology, founded by Edmund Husserl, is one of the most influential German philosophical movements of the 20th century.

column6: Hermeneutik beschäftigt sich mit der Interpretation von Texten.
column7: Hermeneutics deals with the interpretation of texts.
column8: 'Sich beschäftigen mit' takes the dative: 'mit der Interpretation' — a common reflexive structure in academia.

column6: Der hermeneutische Zirkel beschreibt das Verstehen als Prozess.
column7: The hermeneutic circle describes understanding as a process.
column8: A philosophical concept holding that the meaning of a whole text and of its individual parts illuminate each other.

column6: Eine GmbH ist eine typische Kapitalgesellschaft.
column7: A GmbH is a typical corporation.
column8: 'Kapitalgesellschaft' contrasts with 'Personengesellschaft' (partnership) in German company law.

column6: Die Firma wurde zur Aktiengesellschaft umgewandelt.
column7: The company was converted into a public limited company.
column8: 'Umgewandelt werden zu' is passive with 'zu' plus dative, a fixed structure for describing a formal conversion.

column6: Der Aufsichtsrat überwacht die Geschäftsführung.
column7: The supervisory board oversees management.
column8: Germany's two-tier system (Vorstand and Aufsichtsrat) separates operational management from strategic oversight.

column6: Der Vorstand trifft die operativen Entscheidungen.
column7: The executive board makes the operational decisions.
column8: 'Treffen' in this sense means 'to make (a decision)': 'eine Entscheidung treffen' is a fixed collocation.

column6: Die Hauptversammlung findet im Mai statt.
column7: The annual general meeting takes place in May.
column8: 'Stattfinden' is separable: 'findet statt' in the present tense, used for formally scheduled events.

column6: Das Unternehmen meldet Insolvenzverfahren an.
column7: The company is filing for insolvency proceedings.
column8: 'Anmelden' is separable and takes the accusative, used in formal administrative and legal contexts.

column6: Die Sanierung des Unternehmens gelang knapp.
column7: The restructuring of the company barely succeeded.
column8: 'Gelingen' takes the dative of the subject who succeeds — a typically inverted construction compared to English 'to manage to'.

column6: Die Liquidität der Firma ist angespannt.
column7: The company's liquidity is strained.
column8: 'Angespannt' comes from 'anspannen' (to tense), used as an adjective for describing a precarious financial situation.

column6: Die Bilanz weist einen Verlust aus.
column7: The balance sheet shows a loss.
column8: 'Ausweisen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to show, indicate (in a document)', common in accounting.

column6: Die Abschreibung verringert den Gewinn.
column7: Depreciation reduces the profit.
column8: 'Verringern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to reduce', a formal inseparable verb in accounting.

column6: Die Firma bildet Rücklagen für schlechte Zeiten.
column7: The company builds up reserves for hard times.
column8: 'Bilden' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to form, build up', a verb common in accounting language.

column6: Die Kapitalflussrechnung zeigt die Zahlungsströme.
column7: The cash flow statement shows the payment flows.
column8: A technical accounting compound: 'Kapitalfluss' (capital flow) + 'Rechnung' (statement).

column6: Diversifikation reduziert das Risiko.
column7: Diversification reduces risk.
column8: 'Reduzieren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to reduce', a standard financial term.

column6: Die Volatilität der Märkte hat zugenommen.
column7: Market volatility has increased.
column8: 'Zunehmen' is separable and means 'to increase', often used in financial language.

column6: Viele fürchten eine neue Spekulationsblase.
column7: Many fear a new speculative bubble.
column8: 'Fürchten' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to fear', a verb common in economic and financial discourse.

column6: Der Konjunkturzyklus beeinflusst die Beschäftigung.
column7: The business cycle affects employment.
column8: 'Beeinflussen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, a formal verb used in economics.

column6: Strukturelle Arbeitslosigkeit ist schwer zu bekämpfen.
column7: Structural unemployment is hard to fight.
column8: 'Schwer zu bekämpfen' takes the infinitive with 'zu', used to express a persistent difficulty.

column6: Automatisierung führt zu Produktivitätssteigerung.
column7: Automation leads to a productivity increase.
column8: 'Führen zu' takes the dative: 'zu Produktivitätssteigerung' — a fixed structure for expressing a consequence.

column6: Deflation kann ebenso schädlich sein wie Inflation.
column7: Deflation can be just as harmful as inflation.
column8: 'Ebenso ... wie' expresses a comparison of equality, the same structure as 'genauso ... wie'.

column6: Die Staatsverschuldung erreicht einen Rekordwert.
column7: National debt is reaching a record level.
column8: 'Erreichen' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a verb common in economic discourse.

column6: Die Schuldenbremse begrenzt die Neuverschuldung.
column7: The debt brake limits new borrowing.
column8: The 'Schuldenbremse' is a German constitutional rule introduced in 2009 that strongly limits the public deficit.

column6: Das Haushaltsdefizit muss reduziert werden.
column7: The budget deficit must be reduced.
column8: 'Reduziert werden' is passive, used to describe a necessary fiscal policy.

column6: Der Staat gewährt Subventionen für erneuerbare Energien.
column7: The state grants subsidies for renewable energy.
column8: 'Gewähren' takes an optional dative and the accusative, a formal verb for granting public benefits.

column6: Marktversagen rechtfertigt staatliches Eingreifen.
column7: Market failure justifies state intervention.
column8: 'Rechtfertigen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to justify', a formal economic-political term.

column6: Umweltverschmutzung ist eine negative Externalität.
column7: Pollution is a negative externality.
column8: 'Externalität' is a technical economics term, referring to the unpriced side effects of an economic activity.

column6: Öffentliche Güter leiden unter dem Trittbrettfahrerproblem.
column7: Public goods suffer from the free-rider problem.
column8: 'Leiden unter' takes the dative: 'unter dem Trittbrettfahrerproblem' — an image drawn from 'hopping on the running board for free'.

column6: Informationsasymmetrie führt oft zu Marktversagen.
column7: Information asymmetry often leads to market failure.
column8: A central concept in economic theory, when one party in a transaction has more information than the other.

column6: Staatliche Rettungspakete schaffen Moral Hazard.
column7: State bailout packages create moral hazard.
column8: A technical term taken directly from English, widely used in German economic literature too.

column6: Man muss die Opportunitätskosten jeder Entscheidung bedenken.
column7: One must consider the opportunity cost of every decision.
column8: 'Bedenken' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to consider, take into account', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Der Grenznutzen sinkt mit steigendem Konsum.
column7: Marginal utility falls as consumption rises.
column8: 'Mit steigendem Konsum' uses the dative, indicating a simultaneous relationship between two variables.

column6: Die Pathogenese dieser Krankheit ist kaum erforscht.
column7: The pathogenesis of this disease is barely researched.
column8: 'Kaum erforscht' means 'barely studied, little explored', often used in medical research language.

column6: Die Ätiologie bleibt in vielen Fällen unklar.
column7: The etiology remains unclear in many cases.
column8: 'Ätiologie' comes from the Greek 'aitia' (cause): the study of the causes of a disease.

column6: Die Differentialdiagnose schließt andere Ursachen aus.
column7: The differential diagnosis rules out other causes.
column8: 'Ausschließen' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to rule out', a common technical medical term.

column6: Der Arzt kann noch keine Prognose stellen.
column7: The doctor can't yet give a prognosis.
column8: 'Eine Prognose stellen' is the standard fixed collocation, like 'eine Diagnose stellen'.

column6: Die Krankheit befindet sich in Remission.
column7: The disease is in remission.
column8: 'Sich befinden in' takes the dative: 'in Remission' — a formal structure for describing a medical state.

column6: Diese Kontraindikation muss beachtet werden.
column7: This contraindication must be observed.
column8: 'Beachtet werden' is passive, common in formal medical and pharmaceutical terminology.

column6: Der Wirkstoff wird langsam freigesetzt.
column7: The active ingredient is released slowly.
column8: 'Freigesetzt werden' is passive, referring to the gradual release of a drug into the body.

column6: Die klinische Studie zeigt vielversprechende Ergebnisse.
column7: The clinical trial shows promising results.
column8: 'Vielversprechend' combines 'viel' and 'versprechen' (to promise): literally 'that which promises a lot'.

column6: Der Placeboeffekt ist wissenschaftlich gut dokumentiert.
column7: The placebo effect is well documented scientifically.
column8: 'Wissenschaftlich gut dokumentiert' is a structure typical of research language, with the adverb before the participle.

column6: Antibiotikaresistenz ist ein wachsendes Problem.
column7: Antibiotic resistance is a growing problem.
column8: 'Wachsend' as a present participle used as an adjective means 'growing', common in medical-health language.

column6: Epidemiologie untersucht die Verbreitung von Krankheiten.
column7: Epidemiology studies the spread of diseases.
column8: 'Untersuchen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, a verb common in scientific contexts.

column6: Die Inzidenz ist in dieser Region hoch.
column7: The incidence rate is high in this region.
column8: 'Inzidenz' is a statistical-epidemiological term measuring the frequency of new cases in a given period.

column6: Die Prävalenz der Krankheit nimmt zu.
column7: The prevalence of the disease is increasing.
column8: Unlike 'Inzidenz' (new cases), 'Prävalenz' measures the total number of existing cases at a given time.

column6: Die Mortalitätsrate ist deutlich gesunken.
column7: The mortality rate has fallen significantly.
column8: 'Deutlich gesunken' means 'fallen significantly', often used in public health statistics.

column6: Neurowissenschaft erklärt viele Verhaltensmuster.
column7: Neuroscience explains many behavior patterns.
column8: 'Neurowissenschaft' combines the Greek prefix 'Neuro-' and 'Wissenschaft' (science), a relatively young field of research.

column6: Die Synapsen übertragen elektrische Signale.
column7: Synapses transmit electrical signals.
column8: 'Übertragen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to transmit', a technical verb common in neuroscience.

column6: Die Plastizität des Gehirns nimmt mit dem Alter ab.
column7: Brain plasticity decreases with age.
column8: 'Abnehmen' is separable and means 'to decrease', common in discourse about cognitive aging.

column6: Kognitive Fähigkeiten verändern sich mit dem Alter.
column7: Cognitive abilities change with age.
column8: 'Kognitiv' is a Latin loanword, a standard term in psychology and neuroscience.

column6: Demenz betrifft immer mehr Menschen weltweit.
column7: Dementia affects more and more people worldwide.
column8: Used in the singular: 'an Demenz leiden' (to suffer from dementia, 'an' + dative). The adjective is 'dement'; Alzheimer's is one form of Demenz.

column6: Neurodegeneration verläuft meist schleichend.
column7: Neurodegeneration usually progresses insidiously.
column8: 'Schleichend' comes from 'schleichen' (to creep), used to describe gradual pathological processes.

column6: Das menschliche Genom wurde 2003 sequenziert.
column7: The human genome was sequenced in 2003.
column8: 'Sequenziert werden' is passive, referring to the completion of the international Human Genome Project.

column6: Manche Mutationen sind harmlos.
column7: Some mutations are harmless.
column8: 'Manche' means 'some, certain', a common indefinite pronoun/adjective in general scientific discourse.

column6: Biotechnologie eröffnet neue medizinische Möglichkeiten.
column7: Biotechnology opens up new medical possibilities.
column8: 'Eröffnen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, meaning 'to open' figuratively or literally.

column6: Nanotechnologie könnte die Medizin revolutionieren.
column7: Nanotechnology could revolutionize medicine.
column8: From Greek 'nános' (dwarf, very small) + 'Technologie'. A nanometre is a billionth of a metre.

column6: Ein Quantencomputer löst manche Probleme viel schneller.
column7: A quantum computer solves some problems much faster.
column8: 'Viel schneller' reinforces the comparative 'schneller' with 'viel', indicating a substantial difference.

column6: Maschinelles Lernen verbessert sich stetig.
column7: Machine learning keeps improving steadily.
column8: 'Sich verbessern' is reflexive and means 'to improve (itself)', often used for technological systems.

column6: Ein neuronales Netz simuliert das menschliche Gehirn.
column7: A neural network simulates the human brain.
column8: 'Simulieren' takes a direct accusative object, a standard technical term in artificial intelligence.

column6: Der Algorithmus braucht einen großen Datensatz.
column7: The algorithm needs a large dataset.
column8: 'Datensatz' combines 'Daten' (data) and 'Satz' (set), a standard technical term in computer science.

column6: Verzerrung in den Daten führt zu falschen Ergebnissen.
column7: Bias in the data leads to false results.
column8: 'Führen zu' takes the dative: 'zu falschen Ergebnissen' — a fixed structure for expressing a negative consequence.

column6: Seine Rhetorik überzeugte das Publikum.
column7: His rhetoric convinced the audience.
column8: 'Überzeugen' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a verb common in persuasive discourse.

column6: Das war natürlich eine rhetorische Frage.
column7: That was of course a rhetorical question.
column8: A question posed not to get an answer but to emphasize a point, a classic rhetorical technique.

column6: Der Redner nutzte eine kraftvolle Anapher.
column7: The speaker used a powerful anaphora.
column8: 'Anapher' is the repetition of a word at the start of successive sentences, a classic rhetorical device used for emphasis.

column6: Der Text appelliert stark an das Pathos.
column7: The text strongly appeals to pathos.
column8: 'Appellieren an' takes the accusative: 'an das Pathos' — a fixed structure in classical rhetorical analysis (ethos, pathos, logos).

column6: Der Redner baut zunächst sein Ethos auf.
column7: The speaker first builds up his ethos.
column8: 'Aufbauen' is separable and takes the accusative: in classical rhetorical analysis, ethos is the speaker's credibility.

column6: Ein Logos-Argument stützt sich auf Fakten.
column7: A logos argument rests on facts.
column8: 'Sich stützen auf' takes the accusative: 'auf Fakten' — the third pillar of classical rhetoric alongside ethos and pathos.

column6: Die Polemik richtet sich gegen die Regierung.
column7: The polemic is directed against the government.
column8: Sharp, aggressive criticism, often personal. The adjective is 'polemisch', the verb 'polemisieren'.

column6: Die Rede geriet zu einer bloßen Invektive.
column7: The speech degenerated into a mere invective.
column8: 'Geraten zu' takes the dative: 'zu einer Invektive' — a fixed structure for describing an unintended degeneration.

column6: Die Ambivalenz seiner Haltung ist offensichtlich.
column7: The ambivalence of his stance is obvious.
column8: 'Offensichtlich' means 'obvious, evident', a formal adjective common in critical analysis.

column6: Sie steckt in einem tiefen Zwiespalt.
column7: She's caught in a deep inner conflict.
column8: 'Stecken in' takes the dative: 'in einem Zwiespalt' — a fixed structure for describing being caught in a difficult situation.

column6: Diese Aussage ist ein Widerspruch in sich.
column7: This statement is a self-contradiction.
column8: 'In sich' reinforces the idea that the contradiction is internal to the statement itself, not external.

column6: Viele erleben in der Lebensmitte eine Sinnkrise.
column7: Many experience an existential crisis at midlife.
column8: 'Sinnkrise' combines 'Sinn' (meaning) and 'Krise' (crisis): the existential crisis tied to the search for meaning.

column6: Entfremdung von der Arbeit ist ein altes Thema.
column7: Alienation from work is an old topic.
column8: A central concept in Karl Marx's philosophy, referring to the separation between the worker and the product of their labor.

column6: Max Weber sprach von der Entzauberung der Welt.
column7: Max Weber spoke of the disenchantment of the world.
column8: A famous concept from German sociologist Max Weber, referring to the growing rationalization of modern society.

column6: Anomie beschreibt den Verlust sozialer Normen.
column7: Anomie describes the loss of social norms.
column8: A sociological concept introduced by Émile Durkheim, referring to the breakdown of shared social norms.

column6: Soziale Kohäsion wird durch Ungleichheit geschwächt.
column7: Social cohesion is weakened by inequality.
column8: 'Geschwächt werden durch' is passive with 'durch' plus accusative, indicating the cause of the weakening.

column6: Marginalisierung betrifft besonders vulnerable Gruppen.
column7: Marginalization especially affects vulnerable groups.
column8: 'Vulnerabel' is a Latin loanword, a formal synonym for 'verletzlich' (vulnerable), common in academic social discourse.

column6: Die Stigmatisierung psychischer Erkrankungen nimmt langsam ab.
column7: The stigmatization of mental illness is slowly decreasing.
column8: 'Abnehmen' is separable and means 'to decrease', used in discourse about shifting social perception.

column6: Selbststigmatisierung erschwert die Genesung.
column7: Self-stigma makes recovery harder.
column8: 'Erschweren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to make difficult', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Das Prekariat wächst in vielen europäischen Ländern.
column7: The precariat is growing in many European countries.
column8: 'Prekariat' is a sociological neologism describing the class of precarious workers, coined in the 2000s.

column6: Manche Soziologen bezweifeln, dass die Klassengesellschaft verschwunden ist.
column7: Some sociologists doubt that class society has disappeared.
column8: 'Bezweifeln, dass' takes a subordinate clause with 'dass', a common structure in critical academic discourse.

column6: Soziale Mobilität ist in manchen Ländern eingeschränkt.
column7: Social mobility is limited in some countries.
column8: 'Eingeschränkt' comes from 'einschränken' (to restrict), used as an adjective to describe a restricted condition.

column6: Der Begriff Habitus stammt von Pierre Bourdieu.
column7: The term habitus comes from Pierre Bourdieu.
column8: A key sociological concept from the Frenchman Bourdieu, much discussed in contemporary German sociology too.

column6: Kulturelles Kapital beeinflusst den Bildungserfolg.
column7: Cultural capital influences educational success.
column8: 'Beeinflussen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, a key term in the sociology of education.

column6: Sozialer Aufstieg ist nicht für alle gleich einfach.
column7: Social ascent isn't equally easy for everyone.
column8: 'Gleich einfach' means 'equally easy', a comparative structure common in discourse about social fairness.

column6: Prekarisierung betrifft zunehmend auch Akademiker.
column7: Precarisation increasingly affects graduates too.
column8: 'Zunehmend' as a present participle used as an adverb means 'increasingly'.

column6: Wir leben im digitalen Zeitalter.
column7: We live in the digital age.
column8: 'Zeitalter' combines 'Zeit' (time) and 'Alter' (age): a formal term for a historical era defined by a distinctive trait.

column6: Die Region erlebt einen tiefgreifenden Umbruch.
column7: The region is undergoing a profound upheaval.
column8: 'Tiefgreifend' combines 'tief' (deep) and 'greifen' (to grasp): literally 'that which grasps deeply', i.e. radical.

column6: Der Erste Weltkrieg war eine historische Zäsur.
column7: World War I was a historical caesura.
column8: 'Zäsur' describes an event marking a clean break between a 'before' and an 'after' in history.

column6: Die Aufklärung markierte einen Epochenwandel.
column7: The Enlightenment marked an epochal shift.
column8: 'Markieren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to mark', used in formal historical analysis.

column6: Der Zeitzeugenbericht liefert wertvolle Einblicke.
column7: The eyewitness account provides valuable insights.
column8: 'Liefern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to provide', a formal verb used in historiography.

column6: Die Geschichtsschreibung ist nie ganz neutral.
column7: Historiography is never entirely neutral.
column8: 'Geschichtsschreibung' combines 'Geschichte' (history) and 'Schreibung' (writing): the way history is told.

column6: Historischer Revisionismus wird kritisch betrachtet.
column7: Historical revisionism is viewed critically.
column8: 'Kritisch betrachtet werden' is passive, common for describing a controversial position in academic debate.

column6: Das kollektive Gedächtnis formt die nationale Identität.
column7: Collective memory shapes national identity.
column8: 'Formen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to shape', a formal sociological-historical term.

column6: Die Aufarbeitung der Vergangenheit dauert Generationen.
column7: Reappraising the past takes generations.
column8: 'Aufarbeitung' comes from 'aufarbeiten' (to work through), a key term in German memory culture.

column6: Die Schuldfrage bleibt bis heute umstritten.
column7: The question of guilt remains disputed to this day.
column8: 'Bis heute' means 'to this day', used to indicate that a historical debate is still open.

column6: Das Konzept der Kollektivschuld wird kontrovers diskutiert.
column7: The concept of collective guilt is controversially debated.
column8: 'Kontrovers diskutiert werden' is passive, common for describing much-debated philosophical or historical topics.

column6: Die Widerstandsbewegung riskierte ihr Leben.
column7: The resistance movement risked their lives.
column8: 'Riskieren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to risk', a verb common in historical discourse about civil courage.

column6: Zivilcourage bedeutet, auch unbequem einzugreifen.
column7: Civil courage means stepping in even when it's uncomfortable.
column8: 'Zivilcourage' combines the Latin 'zivil' and the French 'courage', a hybrid compound much used in German civic education.

column6: Die Aufklärung prägte das moderne Europa.
column7: The Enlightenment shaped modern Europe.
column8: 'Aufklärung' means both the historical philosophical movement and simply 'clarification' in other contexts.

column6: Kant setzte großes Vertrauen in die Vernunft.
column7: Kant placed great trust in reason.
column8: 'Vertrauen setzen in' takes the accusative: 'in die Vernunft' — a fixed structure in philosophical discourse.

column6: Kant definierte Aufklärung als Ausgang aus der Mündigkeit.
column7: Kant defined Enlightenment as the exit from immaturity.
column8: Kant described Enlightenment as the move from 'selbstverschuldeten Unmündigkeit' (self-incurred immaturity) to 'Mündigkeit', the autonomy of thought.

column6: Der Fortschrittsglaube des 19. Jahrhunderts wurde erschüttert.
column7: 19th-century belief in progress was shaken.
column8: 'Erschüttert werden' is passive, common for describing a collective crisis of faith in a historical idea.

column6: Zivilisationskritik ist ein wiederkehrendes Thema.
column7: Critique of civilization is a recurring theme.
column8: 'Wiederkehrend' comes from 'wiederkehren' (to return), used as an adjective for a theme recurring over time.

column6: Viele beklagen die Entfremdung von der Natur.
column7: Many lament the alienation from nature.
column8: 'Beklagen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to lament, deplore', a formal verb used for cultural critiques.

column6: Eine Rückbesinnung auf alte Werte findet statt.
column7: A reflective return to old values is taking place.
column8: 'Rückbesinnung auf' takes the accusative: 'auf alte Werte' — a fixed structure for describing a conscious return to a principle.

column6: Die Region hat eine geopolitisch wichtige Lage.
column7: The region has a geopolitically important location.
column8: 'Geopolitisch' combines 'Geo-' (earth) and 'politisch' (political), a key term in international relations.

column6: Das internationale Machtgefüge verändert sich.
column7: The international power structure is changing.
column8: 'Machtgefüge' combines 'Macht' (power) and 'Gefüge' (structure, order), a key term in political science.

column6: Das Bündnis besteht seit über siebzig Jahren.
column7: The alliance has existed for over seventy years.
column8: 'Bestehen seit' takes the dative after 'seit', a standard structure for expressing how long something has existed.

column6: Die Souveränität des Staates wird respektiert.
column7: The state's sovereignty is respected.
column8: 'Respektiert werden' is passive, common in international diplomatic language.

column6: Die Schweiz bewahrt traditionell ihre Neutralität.
column7: Switzerland traditionally maintains its neutrality.
column8: 'Bewahren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to maintain, preserve', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Die EU verhängt neue Sanktionen.
column7: The EU is imposing new sanctions.
column8: 'Verhängen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to impose (a penalty or measure)', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Diplomatie erfordert Geduld und Fingerspitzengefühl.
column7: Diplomacy requires patience and tact.
column8: 'Erfordern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to require', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Ein Waffenstillstand wurde vereinbart.
column7: A ceasefire was agreed upon.
column8: 'Vereinbart werden' is passive, common in diplomatic and journalistic language about conflicts.

column6: Die Friedensverhandlungen kommen nur langsam voran.
column7: The peace negotiations are only moving forward slowly.
column8: 'Vorankommen' is separable and means 'to progress, move forward', often used for slow, difficult processes.

column6: Der Roman wechselt die Erzählperspektive.
column7: The novel changes its narrative perspective.
column8: 'Erzählperspektive' combines 'erzählen' (to narrate) and 'Perspektive' (perspective), a key term in narratology.

column6: Ein allwissender Erzähler kennt alle Gedanken der Figuren.
column7: An omniscient narrator knows all the characters' thoughts.
column8: 'Allwissend' combines 'all-' (all) and 'wissend' (knowing), a standard term in literary theory.

column6: Der innere Monolog zeigt ihre wahren Gefühle.
column7: The interior monologue shows her true feelings.
column8: A narrative technique that makes a character's thoughts accessible without the narrator's mediation.

column6: Der Autor durchbricht bewusst die Chronologie.
column7: The author deliberately breaks chronology.
column8: 'Durchbrechen' takes a direct accusative object and is typically inseparable figuratively, separable literally.

column6: Die Vorausdeutung im ersten Kapitel ist subtil.
column7: The foreshadowing in the first chapter is subtle.
column8: 'Vorausdeutung' combines 'voraus' (in advance) and 'Deutung' (interpretation, indication), a technical narratological term.

column6: Die Rückblende erklärt ihre Motivation.
column7: The flashback explains her motivation.
column8: 'Rückblende' combines 'zurück' (back) and 'Blende' (aperture, effect): a term originally from film.

column6: Das Meer ist ein Leitmotiv in diesem Roman.
column7: The sea is a leitmotif in this novel.
column8: 'Leitmotiv' combines 'leiten' (to lead) and 'Motiv' (motif), a musical term (Wagner) also applied to literature.

column6: Zwei Erzählstränge verlaufen parallel.
column7: Two narrative strands run in parallel.
column8: 'Verlaufen' means 'to proceed, unfold', often used to describe the development of a complex plot.

column6: Die Rahmenhandlung verbindet alle Episoden.
column7: The frame story connects all the episodes.
column8: 'Rahmenhandlung' combines 'Rahmen' (frame) and 'Handlung' (plot): the structure that encloses multiple stories.

column6: Ein unzuverlässiger Erzähler macht den Leser misstrauisch.
column7: An unreliable narrator makes the reader suspicious.
column8: 'Misstrauisch machen' means 'to make suspicious', a common causative structure for describing effects on a reader.

column6: Textkohärenz entsteht durch logische Verknüpfungen.
column7: Textual coherence arises from logical connections.
column8: 'Entstehen durch' takes the accusative after 'durch', indicating the means by which something is generated.

column6: Konnektoren helfen, Kohärenz herzustellen.
column7: Connectors help establish coherence.
column8: 'Herstellen' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to create, produce', used in text-linguistic analysis.

column6: Diese Textsorte hat feste Konventionen.
column7: This text type has fixed conventions.
column8: 'Textsorte' combines 'Text' (text) and 'Sorte' (type, kind), a technical term in text linguistics.

column6: Das Wort hat eine negative Konnotation.
column7: The word has a negative connotation.
column8: As opposed to 'Denotation' (literal meaning), 'Konnotation' describes a word's emotional associations.

column6: Die Denotation eines Wortes ist sein wörtlicher Sinn.
column7: The denotation of a word is its literal meaning.
column8: 'Denotation' and 'Konnotation' form a classic conceptual pair in linguistic semantics.

column6: Er wechselt geschickt das sprachliche Register.
column7: He skillfully switches the linguistic register.
column8: 'Register' denotes a language's level of formality, adapted to the social context of communication.

column6: Umgangssprache unterscheidet sich stark vom Schriftdeutschen.
column7: Colloquial language differs greatly from written German.
column8: 'Sich unterscheiden von' takes the dative: 'vom Schriftdeutschen' — a fixed structure for linguistic comparisons.

column6: Die Fachsprache der Juristen ist oft schwer verständlich.
column7: Lawyers' technical language is often hard to understand.
column8: 'Schwer verständlich' implicitly carries an understood 'zu', meaning 'hard to understand'.

column6: Amtsdeutsch gilt als besonders kompliziert.
column7: Bureaucratic German is considered especially complicated.
column8: 'Gelten als' takes the nominative/accusative after 'als', a fixed structure for expressing a widespread reputation.

column6: Manche Fremdwörter wirken gestelzt.
column7: Some loanwords sound stilted.
column8: 'Gestelzt' means 'stilted, pompous', used to criticize an excessive use of foreign words.

column6: 'Fenster' ist ein altes Lehnwort aus dem Lateinischen.
column7: 'Fenster' is an old loanword from Latin.
column8: Unlike 'Fremdwort' (perceived as foreign), a 'Lehnwort' is fully assimilated phonetically and orthographically.

column6: Sprachwandel ist ein natürlicher Prozess.
column7: Language change is a natural process.
column8: 'Sprachwandel' combines 'Sprache' (language) and 'Wandel' (change), a phenomenon studied by historical linguistics.

column6: Sprachpurismus lehnt Anglizismen oft ab.
column7: Language purism often rejects anglicisms.
column8: 'Ablehnen' is separable and takes the accusative, used to describe the rejection of foreign linguistic elements.

column6: Viele Anglizismen haben sich im Deutschen etabliert.
column7: Many anglicisms have become established in German.
column8: 'Sich etablieren' is reflexive and means 'to become established', used to describe linguistic integration.

column6: Sprachwissenschaftler beobachten diesen Trend genau.
column7: Linguists are closely observing this trend.
column8: 'Beobachten' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, a verb common in research language.

column6: Die Standardsprache dient als gemeinsame Norm.
column7: The standard language serves as a common norm.
column8: 'Dienen als' takes the nominative after 'als' and means 'to serve as', a common use with 'dienen'.

column6: Sie arbeitet akribisch an jedem Detail.
column7: She works meticulously on every detail.
column8: 'Akribisch' comes from the Greek 'akribeia' (precision), a high-register term for describing extreme care.

column6: Diese Technologie gilt als obsolet.
column7: This technology is considered obsolete.
column8: 'Obsolet' is a Latin loanword, a formal synonym for 'veraltet' (outdated), used in technical and academic contexts.

column6: Die finanzielle Lage ist prekär.
column7: The financial situation is precarious.
column8: 'Prekär' is a loanword from French, used to describe an unstable, at-risk situation.

column6: Das ist ein gravierender Fehler.
column7: That's a grave mistake.
column8: 'Gravierend' comes from the verb 'gravieren' (to engrave), used figuratively for mistakes of great weight.

column6: Die Antwort war kurz und prägnant.
column7: The answer was short and to the point.
column8: 'Prägnant' describes a clear, essential expressive style, highly valued in formal German writing.

column6: Das ist eine fundierte Analyse.
column7: That's a well-founded analysis.
column8: 'Fundiert' comes from 'Fundament' (foundation), the past participle of 'fundieren' used as an adjective.

column6: Sein Argument ist logisch kohärent.
column7: His argument is logically coherent.
column8: 'Kohärent' is a Latin loanword, used in logical-argumentative contexts to describe internal consistency.

column6: Dieses Argument ist nicht stichhaltig.
column7: This argument isn't valid.
column8: 'Stichhaltig' combines 'Stich' (jab, thrust) and 'halten' (to hold): an argument that 'holds up' against criticism.

column6: Durch den neuen Beweis wird das Argument hinfällig.
column7: With the new evidence, the argument becomes invalid.
column8: 'Hinfällig werden' means 'to become null, lapse', often used in legal and argumentative contexts.

column6: Seine Methoden sind fragwürdig.
column7: His methods are questionable.
column8: 'Fragwürdig' combines 'Frage' (question) and 'würdig' (worthy): literally 'worthy of being questioned'.

column6: Diese Bedingung ist unabdingbar.
column7: This condition is indispensable.
column8: 'Unabdingbar' combines the negative 'un-' and 'abdingen' (to waive a right): literally 'that which cannot be waived'.

column6: Das führt unweigerlich zu Konflikten.
column7: That inevitably leads to conflicts.
column8: 'Unweigerlich' combines the negative 'un-' and 'sich weigern' (to refuse): that which cannot be refused, i.e. is inevitable.

column6: Nicht jede Krise führt zwangsläufig zum Untergang.
column7: Not every crisis necessarily leads to downfall.
column8: 'Zwangsläufig' combines 'Zwang' (compulsion) and 'Lauf' (course): a forced course of events with no alternative.

column6: Wir nehmen viele Reize unterschwellig wahr.
column7: We perceive many stimuli subliminally.
column8: 'Wahrnehmen' is separable and takes a direct accusative object, a technical verb used in perceptual psychology.

column6: Die Bedeutung dieser Erfindung ist kaum zu überschätzen.
column7: The importance of this discovery can hardly be overestimated.
column8: 'Kaum zu + infinitive' expresses an almost absolute impossibility or difficulty, an elegant structure of formal register.

column6: Das lässt sich schwerlich bestreiten.
column7: That can hardly be disputed.
column8: 'Schwerlich' is a literary variant of 'kaum' or 'schwer', typical of formal written register.

column6: Niemand kann diese Tatsache bestreiten.
column7: No one can dispute this fact.
column8: 'Bestreiten' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, a formal verb used in arguments and debates.

column6: Der Anwalt ficht das Urteil an.
column7: The lawyer is challenging the verdict.
column8: 'Anfechten' is separable and takes the accusative, a formal legal term for contesting an official decision.

column6: Die neuen Daten entkräften seine These.
column7: The new data refutes his thesis.
column8: 'Entkräften' combines the privative 'ent-' and 'Kraft' (strength): literally 'to strip an argument of its force'.

column6: Musik untermalt die dramatische Szene.
column7: Music underscores the dramatic scene.
column8: 'Untermalen' comes from 'Malen' (to paint): literally 'to paint underneath', giving an evocative accompaniment.

column6: Diese Maßnahme konterkariert das eigentliche Ziel.
column7: This measure counteracts the actual goal.
column8: 'Konterkarieren' is a loanword from French, used in high register for an effect contrary to what was intended.

column6: Korruption unterminiert das Vertrauen der Bürger.
column7: Corruption undermines citizens' trust.
column8: 'Unterminieren' is a loanword from French/Latin, a formal synonym for 'untergraben' (to undermine).

column6: Schöne Worte kaschieren oft die Realität.
column7: Pretty words often mask reality.
column8: 'Kaschieren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to skillfully hide', often with a critical connotation.

column6: Der Bericht beschönigt die tatsächlichen Zahlen.
column7: The report glosses over the actual figures.
column8: 'Beschönigen' takes a direct accusative object, often criticized in investigative journalism for data manipulation.

column6: Man sollte diese Gefahr nicht verharmlosen.
column7: This danger shouldn't be downplayed.
column8: 'Verharmlosen' comes from 'harmlos' (harmless): literally 'to render harmless', often used critically.

column6: Die Presse dramatisiert oft die Lage.
column7: The press often dramatizes the situation.
column8: 'Dramatisieren' is the opposite of 'verharmlosen': exaggerating the importance or severity of an event.

column6: Das Thema wird politisch instrumentalisiert.
column7: The issue is being politically instrumentalized.
column8: 'Instrumentalisiert werden' is passive, used critically to describe an argument's exploitation for other ends.

column6: Der Künstler erfasst den Zeitgeist perfekt.
column7: The artist captures the zeitgeist perfectly.
column8: 'Erfassen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to grasp (conceptually)', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Manche sehen 2001 als Epochenbruch.
column7: Some see 2001 as an epochal break.
column8: 'Epochenbruch' combines 'Epoche' (era) and 'Bruch' (break), a term for an event marking the clean end of an era.

column6: Soziale Medien prägen das Kollektivbewusstsein.
column7: Social media shapes collective consciousness.
column8: 'Prägen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to shape, deeply characterize', a formal verb.

column6: Massenpsychologie erklärt kollektive Panik.
column7: Mass psychology explains collective panic.
column8: 'Massenpsychologie' combines 'Masse' (mass) and 'Psychologie' (psychology), a field already studied by Gustave Le Bon.

column6: Der Herdentrieb beeinflusst Investitionsentscheidungen.
column7: Herd instinct influences investment decisions.
column8: 'Herdentrieb' combines 'Herde' (herd) and 'Trieb' (instinct), often used in behavioral economics and finance.

column6: Gruppendynamik beeinflusst jede Teamentscheidung.
column7: Group dynamics influence every team decision.
column8: 'Beeinflussen' isn't separable and takes a direct accusative object, a technical term in social psychology.

column6: Konformitätsdruck unterdrückt oft abweichende Meinungen.
column7: Pressure to conform often suppresses dissenting opinions.
column8: 'Unterdrücken' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to suppress', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Das Meinungsklima hat sich merklich verändert.
column7: The climate of opinion has noticeably changed.
column8: 'Merklich' means 'noticeably', a formal adverb used for perceptible changes.

column6: Die Schweigespirale erklärt, warum Minderheitsmeinungen verstummen.
column7: The spiral of silence explains why minority opinions go quiet.
column8: A sociological concept from the German Elisabeth Noelle-Neumann, very influential in political communication studies.

column6: Soziale Netzwerke schaffen oft Echokammern.
column7: Social networks often create echo chambers.
column8: 'Echokammer' is a metaphor taken from acoustics, applied to online information polarization.

column6: Die Filterblase verengt den Horizont.
column7: The filter bubble narrows one's horizon.
column8: Compound of 'Filter' + 'Blase' (bubble); a calque of English 'filter bubble', popularised by Eli Pariser in 2011.

column6: Die politische Polarisierung nimmt zu.
column7: Political polarization is increasing.
column8: 'Zunehmen' is separable and means 'to increase', very common in discourse about political fragmentation.

column6: Online-Radikalisierung ist schwer zu bekämpfen.
column7: Online radicalization is hard to combat.
column8: 'Schwer zu bekämpfen' takes the infinitive with 'zu', used to express a persistent challenge.

column6: Die Verrohung der Sprache im Netz besorgt viele.
column7: The coarsening of language online worries many.
column8: 'Verrohung' comes from 'roh' (raw, coarse): the progressive decline in the civility of public discourse.

column6: Hetze im Internet ist strafbar.
column7: Incitement online is a punishable offense.
column8: 'Strafbar' means 'punishable by law', a formal adjective indicating a criminal offense.

column6: Der Post löste einen regelrechten Shitstorm aus.
column7: The post triggered a real online backlash.
column8: 'Auslösen' is separable and takes the accusative, meaning 'to trigger', much used in the context of social media.

column6: Cancel Culture wird kontrovers diskutiert.
column7: Cancel culture is controversially debated.
column8: A direct loanword from English, widely used unchanged in contemporary German public debate.

column6: Manche kritisieren einen zu engen Meinungskorridor.
column7: Some criticize too narrow a range of acceptable opinion.
column8: 'Meinungskorridor' describes the spectrum of opinions deemed socially acceptable in a debate.

column6: Es sollte keine Denkverbote geben.
column7: There shouldn't be thought taboos.
column8: 'Denkverbot' combines 'Denken' (thought) and 'Verbot' (prohibition): an idea deemed unacceptable to express.

column6: Framing beeinflusst, wie wir Nachrichten verstehen.
column7: Framing influences how we understand news.
column8: 'Beeinflussen, wie' takes a subordinate clause with 'wie', a common structure for describing effects on perception.

column6: Agenda-Setting bestimmt, worüber wir sprechen.
column7: Agenda-setting determines what we talk about.
column8: A communication theory holding that media don't tell us what to think, but determine what we think about.

column6: Der Fall erregte große mediale Aufmerksamkeit.
column7: The case drew great media attention.
column8: 'Erregen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to arouse', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Reizüberflutung durch Medien ist ein modernes Problem.
column7: Sensory overload from media is a modern problem.
column8: 'Reizüberflutung' combines 'Reiz' (stimulus) and 'Überflutung' (flooding): the excess of sensory/informational input.

column6: Viele suchen digitale Entgiftung im Urlaub.
column7: Many seek a digital detox on vacation.
column8: 'Entgiftung' comes from 'Gift' (poison): literally 'removing the poison', applied metaphorically to digital devices.

column6: Klimagerechtigkeit fordert globale Solidarität.
column7: Climate justice demands global solidarity.
column8: 'Fordern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to demand', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Generationengerechtigkeit betrifft auch die Rentenpolitik.
column7: Intergenerational justice also concerns pension policy.
column8: 'Betreffen' takes a direct accusative object with no preposition, used to link a principle to a policy area.

column6: Ressourcenknappheit verschärft internationale Konflikte.
column7: Resource scarcity intensifies international conflicts.
column8: 'Verschärfen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to intensify', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Umweltbewusstsein wächst besonders bei jungen Menschen.
column7: Environmental awareness is growing especially among young people.
column8: 'Wachsen' is a strong irregular verb: 'wuchs, gewachsen', often used for growing social trends.

column6: Klimaskeptiker bezweifeln den menschlichen Einfluss.
column7: Climate sceptics doubt human influence.
column8: 'Bezweifeln' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to doubt', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Der Klimawandel gilt als Konsenswissenschaft.
column7: Climate change is considered a matter of scientific consensus.
column8: 'Gelten als' takes the nominative after 'als', a fixed structure for expressing a widely shared reputation.

column6: Städte entwickeln Anpassungsstrategien gegen Hitzewellen.
column7: Cities are developing adaptation strategies against heat waves.
column8: 'Gegen' always takes the accusative, used here to indicate what a strategy is directed against.

column6: Klimafolgenforschung liefert wichtige Prognosen.
column7: Climate impact research provides important projections.
column8: 'Liefern' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to provide', a verb common in scientific discourse.

column6: Wissenschaftler warnen vor einem globalen Kipppunkt.
column7: Scientists are warning of a global tipping point.
column8: 'Warnen vor' takes the dative: 'vor einem Kipppunkt' — a common fixed structure for scientific warnings.

column6: Mehrere planetare Grenzen sind bereits überschritten.
column7: Several planetary boundaries have already been crossed.
column8: 'Überschritten' comes from 'überschreiten' (to cross), an inseparable verb used in ecological and legal contexts.

column6: Suffizienz bedeutet, bewusst weniger zu konsumieren.
column7: Sufficiency means consciously consuming less.
column8: 'Suffizienz' is a technical sustainability term, distinct from 'Effizienz' (doing more with less) and 'Konsistenz' (changing materials).

column6: Postwachstumsökonomie stellt das BIP-Wachstum infrage.
column7: The post-growth economy calls GDP growth into question.
column8: 'Infrage stellen' means 'to call into question', a fixed phrase also written 'in Frage stellen'.

column6: Konsumkritik hat eine lange intellektuelle Tradition.
column7: Critique of consumerism has a long intellectual tradition.
column8: 'Konsumkritik' combines 'Konsum' (consumption) and 'Kritik' (critique), a line of thought going back at least to the early 20th century.

column6: Der Wachstumszwang der Wirtschaft wird zunehmend kritisiert.
column7: The economy's growth imperative is being increasingly criticized.
column8: 'Wachstumszwang' combines 'Wachstum' (growth) and 'Zwang' (compulsion), a critical concept regarding mainstream economics.

column6: Das Buch fördert die Selbstermächtigung der Leserin.
column7: The book promotes the female reader's self-empowerment.
column8: 'Selbstermächtigung' combines 'selbst' (self) and 'Ermächtigung' (authorization, power), a key term in feminist discourse.

column6: Die Emanzipation der Frauen war ein langer Prozess.
column7: Women's emancipation was a long process.
column8: 'Emanzipation' comes from the Latin 'emancipare' (to free from paternal guardianship), today used in a broad social sense.

column6: Selbstbestimmung ist ein Grundrecht.
column7: Self-determination is a fundamental right.
column8: 'Selbstbestimmung' combines 'selbst' and 'Bestimmung' (determination), used both individually and for peoples and nations.

column6: Viele lehnen sich gegen Fremdbestimmung auf.
column7: Many rebel against external determination.
column8: 'Sich auflehnen gegen' takes the accusative: 'gegen Fremdbestimmung' — a fixed structure for expressing rebellion.

column6: Autonomiebestrebungen prägen viele Regionen Europas.
column7: Strivings for autonomy shape many regions of Europe.
column8: 'Prägen' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to shape, characterize', often used in political analysis.

column6: Selbstwirksamkeit stärkt die psychische Widerstandskraft.
column7: Self-efficacy strengthens psychological resilience.
column8: 'Selbstwirksamkeit' is a key psychological term, coined by psychologist Albert Bandura, translated from the English 'self-efficacy'.

column6: Ihre innere Widerstandskraft beeindruckte alle.
column7: Her inner resilience impressed everyone.
column8: 'Widerstandskraft' combines 'Widerstand' (resistance) and 'Kraft' (strength), a near-formal synonym for 'Resilienz'.

column6: Selbstoptimierung wird zunehmend kritisch gesehen.
column7: Self-optimisation is increasingly viewed critically.
column8: 'Kritisch gesehen werden' is passive, used to describe an increasingly negative social perception.

column6: Selbstausbeutung ist unter Selbstständigen verbreitet.
column7: Self-exploitation is widespread among the self-employed.
column8: 'Verbreitet sein unter' takes the dative: 'unter Selbstständigen' — a structure for describing a phenomenon widespread within a group.

column6: Sie befand sich in einem völligen Erschöpfungszustand.
column7: She was in a state of total exhaustion.
column8: 'Sich befinden in' takes the dative, a formal structure for describing a prolonged state.

column6: Trotz des Erfolgs spürte er eine innere Leere.
column7: Despite the success, he felt an inner emptiness.
column8: 'Trotz' takes the genitive or, colloquially, the dative, used to express a contrast between appearance and feeling.

column6: Arbeit dient vielen zur Sinnstiftung.
column7: For many, work serves as a source of meaning.
column8: 'Dienen zu' takes the dative: 'zur Sinnstiftung' — a fixed structure for expressing something's purpose.

column6: Religion diente historisch der Kontingenzbewältigung.
column7: Historically, religion served to cope with contingency.
column8: A complex sociological-theological term, referring to how humans deal with life's unpredictability.

column6: Ihr Reflexionsvermögen zeichnet sie aus.
column7: Her capacity for reflection sets her apart.
column8: 'Auszeichnen' is separable and takes the accusative: 'zeichnet aus' means 'to distinguish, set apart'.

column6: Ein gutes Urteilsvermögen ist im Beruf unerlässlich.
column7: Good judgement is essential in the profession.
column8: Combines 'Urteil' (judgement) and 'Vermögen' (ability): being able to assess sensibly. A more literary synonym is 'Urteilskraft'.

column6: Richter müssen Unvoreingenommenheit wahren.
column7: Judges must maintain impartiality.
column8: 'Wahren' takes a direct accusative object and means 'to maintain, preserve', a formal inseparable verb.

column6: Aufrichtigkeit ist die Basis jeder echten Beziehung.
column7: Sincerity is the basis of every genuine relationship.
